what_it_does: Large antenna arrays (phased arrays) steer radio beams electronically without moving. When hundreds of antennas sit close together, they interfere with each other electromagnetically, changing how each antenna sees the world (its impedance). This mismatch, called VSWR (voltage standing-wave ratio), causes power amplifiers feeding the antennas to lose power, gain flatness, and efficiency—and breaks the array's calibration. This paper presents a power amplifier using complex-cascode LC-neutralization: a special topology that stays robust across a 4-to-1 range of impedance variations, maintaining steady output power, flat gain curve, and high efficiency regardless of frequency, beam angle, or antenna position in the array.
